messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: layout of tests (source files)
parts:
I suggest we rearrange our test files into subdirectories like:
src/test/unit
src/test/distribution
src/test/model
...

Here are a couple reasons:

* The physical layout would clarify which tests belong to which makefile targets. Right now, some of the targets, like test-distributions, are in the src/test/ folder, but excluded by hand from the test-unit target.

* This will allow us to expand to Windows, Hotfoot, and Travis-CI specific tests. Our Windows toolchain is unable to handle the templating required for forward-mode auto-diff, so we need to find a way to exclude tests if we want to keep using our Jenkins box for continuous integration.


If anyone knows of a better or more standard way of organizing tests, please respond.



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] layout of tests (source files)
parts:
Sounds good to me. I'm all for transparency
based on consistent naming conventions and
directories corresponding to tasks.

Also, you're so fast at moving mountains of code,
you can just move them again later if you figure
out a better way to do it. I'm guessing like
everything else that the right answer is going to
depend on scale. I see our test suites continuing
to grow in the future. For instance, integrators
may be another thing like models that require
their own directory/target.

- Bob
